sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record and reference list for seru1244 (8 refs; Glottolog's most extensive description = Khairunisa 2015).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: Khairunisa 2015 (MA thesis, affixation), Anceaux 1961, Smits & Voorhoeve 1992 (wordlists), Voorhoeve 1975, Galis 1955, Fabritius 1855, de Clercq 1893.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David C. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera-West New Guinea. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Serui-Laut stress statement; Serui-Laut data (from Slump's ms) used only for segmental sound correspondences (ch. 4). Sec. 5.4 (pp. 117-118) reconstructs penultimate stress for Proto-SHWNG from descriptions of Buli, Sawai, Taba, Ambai, Wandamen, Waropen, Warembori; Serui-Laut is not among the languages with a stress description. p. 24: 'For Serui-Laut, there is an unpublished sketch and wordlist (Slump 1924-38).'

sources.citation: Silzer, Peter J. 1983. Ambai: an Austronesian language of Irian Jaya, Indonesia. PhD dissertation, ANU. (Proto-Western-Yapen chapter uses Serui-Laut data from Anceaux.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stress described for Ambai only (penultimate); Serui-Laut appears only in lexicostatistics and segmental correspondence sets; no Serui-Laut stress remark.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David (ed.). Lexifier online database: 'Serui-Laut wordlist', 393 entries keyed from Slump, F. 1924-38, Grammatica en woordenlijst van de Seroei-Laut taal (Het Utrechts Archief).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only; the Serui-Laut forms carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily. 2017. Papuan-Austronesian language contact on Yapen Island: A preliminary account. NUSA 62: 101-155.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; the word 'stress' does not occur. Serui-Laut lexical data cited from Slump (1924-38) and Anceaux (1992); brief note that Ambai and Serui-Laut added /ɸ/ to the inventory.

sources.citation: Anceaux, J.C. 1961. The linguistic situation in the islands of Yapen, Kurudu, Nau and Miosnum, New Guinea. Verhandelingen KITLV 35. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Serui-Laut. Section K (p. 8) covers location, speaker numbers and the possessive system only; p. 14 (transcription of the comparative word-list): 'Stress-accent, vowel pitch and vowel length (part of the accentual system in many of these languages) are not indicated.' The only accent remark in the book concerns Papuma (p. 7: word accent is distinctive).
